name: Mazzy Star
label: Rough Trade
lede: A Paisley Underground guitarist and a teenage folk singer from East LA turned a contract-filler for a dead band into Mazzy Star, had a platinum record by accident, and found interviews and stages equally hard going.

hero.by: Mazzy Star in London, June 2012. Photo: Paul Hudson, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Paisley roots and a demo tape
eras.text: David Roback was one of the architects of LA's Paisley Underground, the early-80s psychedelic revival. Hope Sandoval, the youngest of ten in a rough part of East LA, was a high-school folk singer who followed his band. A demo tape and a walkout in London put them together.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mazzy Star · BBC News · The Guardian
years.h: Roback and his brother Steven start the Rain Parade
years.p: [[Rain Parade|59b6510e-f7f1-4631-be8f-0c493db2502d]] becomes a Paisley Underground mainstay. Before that, the BBC notes, David played in Unconscious with Steven and future Bangles singer Susanna Hoffs.
years.xp: Roback was an outsider from the start. "My hobbies were psychiatry and history," he once said. "I'd psychoanalyse my friends." He studied art at Berkeley before the LA scene took over.

years.h: Roback leaves the Rain Parade and forms Clay Allison with Kendra Smith
years.p: Smith, his girlfriend at the time, had played bass in [[The Dream Syndicate|8577c385-d06a-4a64-b4e7-6ebf25f2cb20]]. After one double A-side, "Fell From the Sun"/"All Souls", they rename the band Opal.

yt: Going Home, Sandoval's duo with Sylvia Gomez
years.h: Sylvia Gomez slips Roback a tape backstage
years.p: After a [[Rain Parade|59b6510e-f7f1-4631-be8f-0c493db2502d]] show in LA, Gomez hands Roback a demo by Going Home, her folk duo with Sandoval. He offers to produce their album.
years.xp:
Sandoval and Gomez had formed Going Home at school, and had played gigs with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]]. Roback thought Sandoval's voice was "really intense and completely unique". The Guardian dates the production offer to 1986; the album was never released.

One Going Home song, Gomez's "Give You My Lovin'", later turned up on Mazzy Star's first album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mazzy Star · The Guardian · NPR
years.h: Kendra Smith walks out on Opal mid-tour, and Sandoval steps in
years.p: Smith quits during a concert in London while Opal are supporting [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]]. Roback brings in Sandoval to finish as the singer.

years.h: Opal's Happy Nightmare Baby comes out on SST
years.p: Released after Smith had gone. [[Keith Mitchell|602949e8-c584-4662-a5dc-5853cfedd18e]], Opal's drummer, stays with Roback into the next band.

eras.title: Opal on paper, Mazzy Star on tape
eras.text: Rough Trade still had Roback under contract for a second Opal album. Two years of touring under the old name gave Sandoval enough of the old songs, and the new band was written fast once she said so.

years.h: Sandoval wants "something completely new", so Ghost Highway is shelved
years.p: The pair had finished a second Opal album of mostly Roback and Smith songs. Sandoval didn't like it, so they cut seven new tracks at Hyde Street Studios in San Francisco and renamed the band Mazzy Star.

years.h: She Hangs Brightly, Mazzy Star's only Rough Trade album
years.p: No instant hit, but alternative radio takes to it. The single, a cover of Slapp Happy's "Blue Flower", reaches No. 29 on Modern Rock.
years.xp:
Roback had no time for the attention. "It's like being popular at school," he said after the album came out. "What does being popular at school mean? It means nothing."

The album went on to sell more than 70,000 copies in the UK, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Rough Trade's US arm folds, and Capitol picks them up within weeks
years.p: Capitol Records reissues She Hangs Brightly with a major label behind it.

eras.title: A slow hit for a band that wouldn't talk
eras.text: So Tonight That I Might See took a year to find its audience, then went platinum on one song. The band handled the attention as little as possible: on stage, in interviews and in their dealings with Capitol.

years.src: Wikipedia: So Tonight That I Might See
years.h: Roback produces So Tonight That I Might See
years.p: Ten songs, all by Sandoval and Roback except [[Love|34ec9a8d-c65b-48fd-bcdd-aad2f72fdb47]]'s "Five String Serenade". The LA Times called it maybe the culmination of the Paisley Underground.
years.xp: Not everyone heard it that way. Rolling Stone found it increasingly monotonous and Robert Christgau called it a dud. Pitchfork later ranked it the second-best dream pop album ever made.
play: So Tonight That I Might See

years.h: Jill Emery joins on bass
years.p: The former [[Hole|1dcc8968-f2cd-441c-beda-6270f70f2863]] bassist plays with Mazzy Star until 1996.

years.cap: Mazzy Star at the Palace, Hollywood, 1994
years.src: Wikipedia: Mazzy Star · The Guardian · BBC News
years.h: "Fade into You" breaks a year after the album came out
years.p: MTV and radio pick it up. It reaches No. 44 on the Hot 100 and No. 3 on Modern Rock, and pulls the album to platinum by April 1995.
years.xp:
Sandoval was no help explaining it. "I think it's a good song," she told the Guardian years later. "I think a lot of our songs are good."

The song kept paying. It turned up on Desperate Housewives and CSI: Miami, and in 2020 Taylor Swift fans heard it in her single "Lover", the BBC noted.

q: Only when shyness is misinterpreted as arrogance.
years.h: "Talk to us!" the crowd shouts, and the band doesn't
years.p: That's how one early-90s journalist put it. Sandoval refused to discuss her lyrics, turned down autographs and hated playing live; one audience got so fed up it chanted at the stage.
years.xp: The Guardian's Dorian Lynskey collected the reputation in 2013: cancelled tours, interview walkouts, long silences. Roback's explanation, twenty years on, was short.

yt: Fade Into You, live at Shoreline Amphitheatre, 1994
years.h: "Fade into You" at Shoreline Amphitheatre
years.p: The band at the height of the song's run, playing to a California amphitheatre crowd in 1994.

years.h: Sandoval sings "Sometimes Always" with the Jesus and Mary Chain
years.p: Her duet with Jim Reid opens Stoned & Dethroned. The Guardian notes she dated William Reid for three years in this period.

years.h: Among My Swan goes acoustic and sells less
years.p: It enters the Billboard 200 at No. 68. "Flowers in December" is their only UK top 40 single, at No. 40.

years.big: "I had to beg to get out of my contract"
q: I had to beg to get out of my contract with Capitol.
years.h: After a five-month tour, Sandoval asks Capitol to let her go
years.p: Sandoval told the LA Times Capitol wanted her working with big producers. She wanted to produce her own music, and the band stopped releasing records.
years.xp:
She said record companies had started chasing bands that would sell seven million records, and sending people to the studio to check they were following the formula. "So we got out."

By 2013 she told the Guardian there had been no unhappiness at all. Roback said they never broke up: "We hang out a lot. We always have. And when we hang out we make music."

eras.title: Not a split, just a long pause
eras.text: Sandoval started a new band and sang for everyone from the Chemical Brothers to Massive Attack. Roback produced, acted once and moved to Norway. They kept recording together and released nothing as Mazzy Star.

years.h: A short European tour, with up to seven new songs a night
years.p: Sandoval says they're for a fourth album to be released independently. Later in 2000 she forms [[Hope Sandoval & the Warm Inventions|23f527e1-74ae-4f7c-94f3-4a5d5f379c51]] with [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]]'s [[Colm Ó Cíosóig|7f69716d-e363-4642-89c8-e2d74e6c456f]].

years.h: Violinist and keyboardist William Cooper dies
years.p: Wikipedia says he died of neuroendocrine cancer.

years.h: Roback joins Sandoval on stage for Bert Jansch's 60th birthday
years.p: At the Queen Elizabeth Hall in London they play "Suzanne" and "All This Remains" with [[Bert Jansch|d7f95537-2b48-403d-9ac2-f1fc7aad0960]]. It's their last stage appearance together until 2012.

years.cap: Sandoval at All Tomorrow's Parties, New York
years.h: "It's true we're still together," Sandoval tells Rolling Stone
years.p: "We're almost finished," she adds, then says she has no idea what that means. The same year a Virgin Media ad puts "Into Dust" on the UK singles chart.

eras.title: Seventeen years between albums
eras.text: Mazzy Star came back the way they'd always worked: a single with no fanfare, a tour, and an album nobody had been allowed to rush. It sounded exactly like them.

years.h: "Common Burn"/"Lay Myself Down", the first new music in 15 years
years.p: A digital double A-side. The blue 7-inch, delayed at the pressing plant, comes out in January 2012.

years.h: First tour since 2000, from Petaluma to Katowice
years.p: Eighteen dates in California and Europe with original members Suki Ewers and Keith Mitchell, plus Ó Cíosóig and pedal steel player Josh Yenne.
years.xp: Mitchell's son Paul played with them, and his band the Brook Lee Catastrophe opened some shows. New songs like "Flying Low" and "Spoon" went into the set. After the last date in August, Roback said the album was finished and would be out "soon".

years.h: Seasons of Your Day reaches No. 24, their best UK chart placing
years.p: Seventeen years after Among My Swan. Bert Jansch recorded his part before his death in 2011.
years.xp: The Guardian interviewed them by Skype, Sandoval in Ireland and Roback in Norway. Asked why they'd waited so long, Sandoval said, "I don't think we were really in the mood to release music." Roback: "We were always recording and writing. We just didn't release any of it publicly."

years.h: "I'm Less Here" and "Things" for Record Store Day
years.p: A 7-inch on Rough Trade, limited to 3,000 copies worldwide.

eras.title: Losing the rhythm section, then Roback
eras.text: Mazzy Star played their last shows under the sails of the Sydney Opera House, with a record dedicated to their drummer. Two years later Roback was gone too.

years.h: Drummer Keith Mitchell dies
years.p: He had played on all four albums, back to Opal. Wikipedia says he died of cancer.

years.cap: Mazzy Star at the Sydney Opera House, June 2018
yt: Clips from the Sydney shows, June 2018
years.h: Three nights at the Sydney Opera House, and the Still EP
years.p: Their first concerts in five years, for Vivid Live. Still, out June 1, is dedicated to Mitchell and stage manager Tom Cashen, who also died in 2017.

years.src: BBC News · Wikipedia: Mazzy Star · NPR
years.h: David Roback dies in Los Angeles at 61
years.p: Wikipedia gives cancer as the cause; his publicist gave none, the BBC reported. [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]] said he'd always loved Roback's music.
years.xp: Susanna Hoffs said he would be "eternally missed". Sleigh Bells' Alexis Krauss: "I don't know what I would do without Fade Into You."
